messages:
Claire H: Heads-up — opening a docs PR to consolidate our function/tool-calling + structured-output guidance. I found a few issues across pages: inconsistent Node/Python snippets, two broken internal links, and no clear guidance for schema resiliency (nullable arrays, union elements, fallback parsing). I pushed a draft branch: https://git.redwood.com/redwood-inference/docs/compare/schema-resilience-draft :eyes:

Sam K: On it. I'll standardize Node + Python snippets to the SDK v1.3 surface. Quick question — do we want to show both promise/async iterator streaming and the simple .create() usage in the same example, or keep them separate?

Claire H: Keep them separate (short examples). Root page should show the canonical shape + validation checklist; then two tiny snippets: one sync-ish and one streaming. Also can you include a small example that demonstrates a function call returning an array of unions (e.g., [Choice|string]) and how to safely parse it?

Sam K: Yep. Drafting snippets now. For the streaming example I'll use the async iterator form (Node):

```js
// Node SDK v1.3 - streaming
const resp = await redwood.responses.stream({
  model: 'x-rw-instruct-1',
  input: prompt,
  stream: true,
});
for await (const chunk of resp) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta ?? '');
}
```

Sam K: And a short non-stream example for the function/tool call (Node):

```js
const out = await redwood.tools.call({
  name: 'summarize',
  args: { text: longText }
});
console.log(out.result);
```

Ravi P: Thanks — one schema note: when showing nullable fields, prefer the explicit union form in examples for clarity, e.g.

```json
"summary": { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "optional short summary" }
```

Ravi P: For arrays-of-unions (which break some naive parsers), show a guardrail example using oneOf + contentMediaType or a discriminant if possible. Example snippet I propose for docs:

```json
"items": {
  "type": "array",
  "items": {
    "oneOf": [
      { "type": "string" },
      { "type": "object", "properties": { "kind": { "const": "choice" }, "label": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["kind","label"] }
    ]
  }
}
```

Ashley M: Copy edits: suggest a small "migration note" section that says "If you use SDK < v1.2, your call surface may return raw strings for function outputs; upgrade or wrap with a JSON.parse+schema-checker." Also: update two links that currently point to /v1-old/structured-output — they should go to /reference/structured-output. I'll add suggested wording in the PR comments. :white_check_mark:

Claire H: Perfect. Also add a short checklist at the top of the page called "Schema resilience checklist" — items:
- prefer union types over ambiguous freeform arrays
- include discriminants for object unions
- show parsing fallback (try parse -> validate -> fallback message)
- give an ergonomic SDK snippet for Node and Python

Sam K: For Python streaming snippet (short):

```py
# Python SDK v1.3 - streaming
async for chunk in client.responses.stream(model='x-rw-instruct-1', input=prompt):
    print(chunk.delta or '', end='')
```

Sam K: For the Python non-stream function call example:

```py
resp = client.tools.call(name='summarize', args={'text': long_text})
print(resp.result)
```

Ravi P: One more guardrail idea: show an example "lenient parser" pattern in the docs (pseudocode) so application authors see a robust approach: try JSON.parse, then pass to a JSON Schema validator (ajv or jsonschema), on failure fall back to plain-text extract with regex or return a friendly error. Short example recommended.

Claire H: Yes — add that pseudocode. Keep it 4 lines max so it doesn't take over the page.

docs-bot: PR opened — #428: "schema resilience + canonical snippets" by claireh (CI: running) https://git.redwood.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/428

docs-bot: CI status — link-checker found 2 broken links in /reference/structured-output/old-examples -> please fix before merge.

Ashley M: I'll push a small commit to the branch that updates the two links and adds the migration note. Also adding a tiny YAML frontmatter example for the docs site showing language=js/py for the code blocks.

Sam K: Will push SDK snippet PR to that branch in ~30m. Tagging @Ravi P for schema review.

Ravi P: I'll review once snippets are in. Also recommend we add one screenshot of the example parsing flow in the console (tiny) — optional.

Claire H: Great coordination — once Ravi + Sam sign off we can merge. After merge: create a follow-up issue to scan other pages for the same old /v1-old/ links (low-effort link sweep).

Ashley M: Done — added link-fix commit and small wording tweak. PR now has 4 commits.

docs-bot: PR #428 — CI passed (link-checker OK, lint OK), ready for review.

Sam K: Snippets live. Leaving one TODO: decide whether to include a brief note about strict vs lenient parsing performance tradeoffs (AJV validation cost). Suggest a single sentence mentioning cost and recommending targeted validation for hot paths.

Claire H: Add that sentence under "Schema resilience checklist" and we're good. I'll merge after a final thumbs from Ravi. :tada:

Ravi P: LGTM. Thumbs up.

Claire H: Merged. Thanks all! :rocket:
